title: Vaccines for adults: who gets what

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on the ACIP adult immunisation schedule. Ages and products change yearly; review before trusting.

questions.q: From what age is a pneumococcal conjugate vaccine recommended for all adults?
questions.why: Lowered from 65 in 2024. Younger adults get it for conditions such as diabetes, chronic heart, lung, liver or kidney disease, smoking, alcohol use disorder and immunocompromise.

questions.q: A 55-year-old has never had a pneumococcal vaccine. Which single option completes the series in one dose?
questions.why: The alternative is PCV15 followed by PPSV23 a year later. PCV13 followed by PPSV23 in the past counts as complete for most adults.

questions.q: The recombinant zoster vaccine is recommended in two doses from what age?
questions.why: And from 19 for immunocompromised adults. It is given regardless of a past episode of shingles or a past live zoster vaccine.

questions.q: Which influenza vaccines are preferred for adults 65 and older?
questions.a: A high-dose, adjuvanted, or recombinant vaccine
d: No vaccine if they had one last year
questions.why: The live attenuated nasal vaccine is licensed only to age 49 and not for pregnant or immunocompromised people. Everyone six months and older is vaccinated every season.

questions.q: How often is a tetanus-containing booster given after the adult Tdap?
questions.why: Either Td or Tdap. A dirty wound more than five years after the last dose gets a booster. Tdap is repeated in every pregnancy.

questions.q: During which weeks of pregnancy is Tdap given?
questions.why: Early in that window is best for passing pertussis antibody to the baby. The RSV vaccine is given at 32 to 36 weeks during the RSV season.

questions.q: Up to what age is HPV vaccination routinely recommended for adults who were not vaccinated earlier?
questions.why: From 27 to 45 it is a shared decision, since most people have already been exposed. Started at 15 or later it is three doses; started before 15, two.

questions.q: Hepatitis B vaccination is now recommended universally for adults up to what age?
questions.why: From 60 it is by risk factor, including diabetes, liver or kidney disease, and healthcare work. No prior testing is required to vaccinate.

questions.q: Who is recommended to receive a single dose of RSV vaccine?
questions.a: All adults 75 and older, and adults 60 to 74 at increased risk
questions.why: It is a single lifetime dose at present, not an annual one. Increased risk means chronic heart or lung disease, diabetes with complications, kidney disease, immunocompromise or frailty.

questions.q: Which vaccines are live and therefore avoided in pregnancy and severe immunocompromise?
questions.why: The recombinant zoster vaccine replaced the live one and is safe in immunocompromise. A woman found non-immune to rubella in pregnancy is vaccinated after delivery.

First-year college students living in dormitories who missed it
Travel to the meningitis belt or the Hajj
questions.why: Microbiologists working with the organism and people with HIV are also on the list. Asplenia also calls for pneumococcal and Haemophilus vaccination.

questions.q: A healthcare worker born in 1985 has no record of MMR and no serology. What is recommended?
questions.a: Two doses of MMR at least 28 days apart
d: No vaccine; anyone born after 1957 is immune
questions.why: Two doses for healthcare workers, students and travellers; one dose for other adults without evidence of immunity. Birth before 1957 is taken as immune for most, but not for healthcare workers.
